prompt.brief: Design a batch and streaming data platform that ingests events from many sources, transforms them reliably, and serves fresh analytical results without losing data during backpressure or worker failure.
successSignals: Separate immutable raw data, replayable events, stateful stream processing, and query-optimized analytical tables.
Explain event-time windows, late data, watermarks, deduplication, schema evolution, and exactly-once effects.
Use one ingestion contract for streaming and batch backfills while isolating noisy tenants and hot keys.
Define data-quality gates, privacy controls, replay, dead-letter handling, and operational freshness metrics.

functional: Ingest events from APIs, message brokers, databases, and object-storage batch drops.
Validate schemas, normalize records, enrich them, and run windowed streaming and historical batch transformations.
Write raw immutable data and curated analytical tables for dashboards, ad-hoc queries, and exports.
Expose pipeline configuration, run status, freshness, quality failures, replay, backfill, and cancellation.
nonFunctional: Acknowledge accepted events after durable ingestion, not after every downstream table is updated.
Target p95 streaming freshness below 10 seconds for healthy partitions and make lag visible.
Preserve ordering where required by a business key while scaling independent partitions in parallel.
Make retries, late events, duplicate delivery, schema changes, partial sink failure, and regional recovery safe.
scaleAssumptions: Ingest 2 million events per second at peak, with records averaging 2 KB and 10x bursts.
Retain raw data for 90 days in object storage and curated data for years in a columnar warehouse.
Largest tenants can dominate a partition, so partition keys may require salting and tenant quotas.
A streaming job has hundreds of partitions and a batch backfill may run thousands of tasks.

metrics.label: Peak ingest rate
metrics.description: Drives broker partitions, network capacity, and admission control.

metrics.label: Streaming freshness
metrics.description: Time from source event timestamp to curated-table availability.

metrics.label: Raw retention
metrics.description: Replay and audit window before data moves to a lower-cost tier.

metrics.label: Quality acceptance
metrics.description: Invalid records are quarantined with reason codes rather than silently dropped.

entities.name: PipelineDefinition
entities.notes: Version definitions immutably so in-flight jobs retain their original contract.

entities.name: RawEvent
entities.notes: Append-only raw data is the replay authority and carries both event and ingestion timestamps.

entities.name: StreamCheckpoint
entities.notes: Offsets and state snapshots advance together through a checkpoint protocol.

entities.name: QualityFinding
entities.notes: Quality failures are queryable and policy decides whether they block publication.

entities.name: DatasetManifest
entities.notes: Consumers pin an atomic manifest for a consistent batch or table snapshot.

apis.contract: { name, sources, schema, transforms, sinks, requestId } -> { pipelineId, version, state }
apis.notes: Validate DAG, connector credentials, schema compatibility, quotas, and sink permissions.

apis.contract: { pipelineId, events[], requestId } -> { accepted, rejected, partitionOffsets }
apis.notes: Deduplicate by source event ID and acknowledge only after broker durability.
Expose event-time progress and per-partition lag rather than one misleading percentage.

apis.contract: { start, end, sinkSnapshot, requestId } -> { runId, state }
apis.notes: Write an isolated output version and atomically promote it after comparison.

apis.contract: { partitions, fromOffsets, reason, requestId } -> { runId, state }
apis.notes: Authorize and rate-limit replay; keep it separate from the live output.

dataFlow.title: Accept and validate source records
dataFlow.description: Connectors authenticate, validate schema versions, attach tenant and time metadata, and quarantine malformed records.

dataFlow.title: Commit the raw event log
dataFlow.description: The ingestion tier writes partitioned replicated records; the response contains accepted offsets and rejection reasons.

dataFlow.title: Process by event time
dataFlow.description: Stream workers checkpoint state, advance watermarks, deduplicate, and close windows according to lateness policy.

dataFlow.title: Publish quality-gated datasets
dataFlow.description: Sinks write immutable fragments, run quality rules, and advance a dataset manifest only when policy passes.

dataFlow.title: Replay, backfill, and observe asynchronously
dataFlow.description: A control plane schedules repair and historical runs while dashboards consume lag, cost, quality, and lineage events.

architecture.title: Batch and streaming data platform reference architecture
architecture.summary: Durable ingestion feeds replayable raw storage and partitioned processing; quality-gated manifests publish curated data to analytical stores.

deepDives.title: Event time and late data
points: Use event_time for business windows and ingestion time for operational lag.
Advance watermarks from partition progress and define allowed lateness.
Route very late records to correction tables instead of silently mutating closed aggregates.

deepDives.title: Exactly-once effects
points: Assume at-least-once delivery and make sinks idempotent with event IDs or window versions.
Checkpoint offsets with state snapshots and fence old workers.
Use an outbox or idempotency key for external APIs.

deepDives.title: Schema and quality
points: Keep compatible schema versions and quarantine incompatible records with reasons.
Run completeness, uniqueness, range, referential, and privacy checks.
Publish quality and lineage with the dataset manifest.

deepDives.title: Backfills and replay
points: Read immutable raw data into isolated output versions.
Compare counts, distributions, and samples before promotion.
Throttle historical work so it cannot starve streaming freshness.

tradeoffs.title: Unified versus separate engines
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use a common programming model while isolating streaming and batch resources.
tradeoffs.caution: A shared engine can let backfills compete with freshness-critical work.

tradeoffs.title: Broker versus object retention
tradeoffs.recommendation: Keep short replay windows in the broker and archive compressed raw data in objects.
tradeoffs.caution: Object replay is cheaper but slower and needs manifest discipline.

tradeoffs.title: Strict versus warning quality gates
tradeoffs.recommendation: Block security, schema, and key failures; warn on non-critical quality issues.
tradeoffs.caution: Overly strict gates freeze consumers while weak gates hide corruption.

tradeoffs.title: Precompute versus raw queries
tradeoffs.recommendation: Precompute common aggregates and retain curated detail for flexible queries.
tradeoffs.caution: Each projection adds compute and freshness obligations.

commonMistakes: Treating ingestion acknowledgement as proof every sink is updated.
Using processing time for event-time windows without a late-data policy.
Claiming broker exactly-once solves duplicate external side effects.
Letting a historical backfill consume all streaming capacity.
Dropping invalid records without quarantine or replay.
Overwriting a live table from a partial backfill.

followUps.question: What if one tenant creates a hot partition?
followUps.answer: Apply quotas, salt or split the key when ordering permits, isolate its workers, and preserve ordering only where required.

followUps.question: How do you recover after state loss?
followUps.answer: Restore the latest checkpoint and replay broker or raw offsets from a safe boundary, then compare before promotion.

followUps.question: How do you handle a breaking schema?
followUps.answer: Quarantine the incompatible version, alert the owner, retain the payload, and activate a compatible parser after review.

followUps.question: How do consumers get a consistent result?
followUps.answer: Expose a manifest and watermark; consumers pin a version instead of reading while fragments are promoted.

rubric.description: The design has durable acceptance, replayable raw data, partitioning, quotas, and clear acknowledgement semantics.
Event time, watermarks, late data, checkpoints, backfills, and isolated execution are addressed.
Schema evolution, quarantine, quality gates, privacy, lineage, and atomic publication are explicit.
Retries, fencing, lag, freshness, cost, recovery, and replay are observable and actionable.
